cohort: 628,878 mother-child pairs from the Taiwan Birth Cohort Study (TBCS) and National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) between 2006 and 2009.
finding: Male gender, maternal asthma, maternal allergic rhinitis, preterm birth, low birth weight, cesarean section, high urbanization level, and a low number of older siblings were independently associated with an increased risk of childhood asthma.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was found to be an independent predictor for childhood asthma (aOR 1.10, 95% CI 1.08-1.13).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was an independent predictor for childhood asthma (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.19).
